guard: a start the re-exec guard refuses leaves the auth-service pid records as it found them: no slot naming the launcher, and no pre-hex record reclaimed
why: #1629 put a refusal in `selfArgv()`, and `startAuthServiceDetached` called it after the pid work.
`claimAuthPidSlot` publishes the slot already holding the launcher's own pid, so a refused start
left a record that reads alive: a retry in the same process skipped the start and went to the
provider's readiness wait, and teardown signalled whichever process held the launcher's pid. The
dead pre-hex record was reclaimed before the refusal as well.
Each ordering has its own mutant. The first restores the order #1641 shipped, with the argv built
inside the `try` after the claim. The second moves only the reclaim back above the guard, which

mutations.name: the pid slot is claimed before the entry is validated, as #1641 shipped it
mutations.cell: the refused start published no pid slot
mutations.expectRed: the refused start published no pid slot

mutations.name: the dead pre-hex record is reclaimed before the entry is validated
mutations.cell: the refused start left the dead pre-hex record where it was
mutations.expectRed: the refused start left the dead pre-hex record where it was
